program_synthesis.object: A program P in a minimal DSL that computes f(x) for all x
program_synthesis.compression_mechanism: If f has low Kolmogorov complexity, P is much smaller than |f|'s truth table. P IS the law — executing P replaces executing f.
assumptions: f has a short program representation
program_synthesis.limits: Rice's theorem: program equivalence is undecidable. Kolmogorov complexity is uncomputable. Synthesis is EXPTIME-hard in general.
program_synthesis.adversarial_attack: f is a random oracle — no short program exists. Synthesis exhausts the search space without finding P.
program_synthesis.verdict: VIABLE — the execution model changes from 'lookup/store' to 'execute program'. This is fundamentally different from GF(2)/Walsh/DFA which are specific program classes. Program synthesis is the GENERAL case.

term_rewriting.object: A rewrite system R = {l_i → r_i} where normal form of term t gives f(t)
term_rewriting.compression_mechanism: Rewrite rules are compact; normal form computation replaces f.
term_rewriting.limits: Confluence is undecidable. Termination is undecidable. Newmann's lemma requires both.
term_rewriting.adversarial_attack: Non-confluent system: different reduction orders produce different results. Non-terminating: rewrite loop.
term_rewriting.verdict: REJECTED — confluence and termination are undecidable. Cannot guarantee correct compression.

abstract_interpretation.object: An over-approximation A of f's semantics in an abstract domain
abstract_interpretation.compression_mechanism: A is cheaper to compute than f, but only gives conservative bounds.
assumptions: Abstract domain is Galois-connected to concrete
abstract_interpretation.limits: False positives: A may say 'possible' when f says 'impossible'. Precision loss is inherent.
abstract_interpretation.adversarial_attack: f has sharp boundaries — abstract interpretation loses all precision.
abstract_interpretation.verdict: REJECTED — it approximates, not compresses. The requirement is EXACT compression, not bounds.

constraint_propagation.object: A CSP (variables, domains, constraints) whose solutions are f's preimages
constraint_propagation.compression_mechanism: Constraints are compact; CSP solving replaces f.
assumptions: f's preimages have structure expressible as constraints
constraint_propagation.limits: CSP solving is NP-hard. Constraint extraction from observations is itself hard.
constraint_propagation.adversarial_attack: f is injective — each preimage is a singleton. CSP = enumeration = no compression.
constraint_propagation.verdict: REJECTED — CSP solving is NP-hard and doesn't change the execution model (still solving, not executing a compact law).

category_theory.object: A universal property (free object, adjunction) that characterizes f
category_theory.compression_mechanism: Universal properties are maximally compact (defined by their uniqueness).
assumptions: f is a functor/morphism with a universal property
category_theory.limits: Most functions don't have universal properties. The abstraction is too high-level for computation.
category_theory.adversarial_attack: f is an arbitrary Boolean function — no universal property exists.
category_theory.verdict: REJECTED — too abstract. Universal properties characterize structure, not arbitrary computations.

topological_data_analysis.object: Persistent homology of f's level sets
topological_data_analysis.compression_mechanism: Betti numbers and persistence diagrams are compact descriptors.
assumptions: f's level sets have topological structure
topological_data_analysis.limits: Boolean functions on {0,1}^d have trivial topology (discrete). No persistent features.
topological_data_analysis.adversarial_attack: Any Boolean function — topology is trivial on discrete spaces.
topological_data_analysis.verdict: REJECTED — Boolean function spaces are discrete; topological methods require continuous spaces.

symbolic_dynamics.object: A shift space Σ and a factor map π: Σ → {0,1} representing f
symbolic_dynamics.compression_mechanism: Shift spaces are defined by forbidden blocks — compact if few forbidden patterns.
assumptions: f is a sliding block code on a shift space
symbolic_dynamics.limits: Most functions are not sliding block codes. Entropy of the shift space may be maximal.
symbolic_dynamics.adversarial_attack: f depends on all d bits — the shift space has maximal entropy = no compression.
symbolic_dynamics.verdict: REJECTED — shift spaces model temporal/sequential systems, not arbitrary Boolean functions.

graph_rewriting.object: A graph G and rewrite rules that transform input graphs to output
graph_rewriting.compression_mechanism: Graph rewrite rules are compact; graph matching replaces f.
graph_rewriting.limits: Subgraph isomorphism is NP-complete. Confluence of graph rewriting is undecidable.
graph_rewriting.adversarial_attack: f operates on flat bit-vectors — no graph structure to exploit.
graph_rewriting.verdict: REJECTED — graph rewriting is for graph-structured inputs, not Boolean functions.

proof_systems.object: A constructive proof P that '∀x, f(x) = y' with a witness extraction function
proof_systems.compression_mechanism: Proof P is compact if f has short derivations. Witness extraction = computation.
proof_systems.limits: Proof complexity lower bounds (Razborov): some functions require exponential proofs.
proof_systems.adversarial_attack: f is a random function — any proof of f's behavior requires Ω(2^d) lines.
proof_systems.verdict: MARGINAL — proof systems ARE programs (Curry-Howard). But proof search is harder than program synthesis. Subsumed by program synthesis.

algorithmic_information_theory.object: The shortest program P* that computes f, found via universal search
algorithmic_information_theory.compression_mechanism: K(f) = |P*|. If K(f) << |truth table|, P* IS the compression.
algorithmic_information_theory.limits: K(f) is uncomputable (Chaitin's theorem). Universal search is O(2^K) — doubly exponential.
algorithmic_information_theory.adversarial_attack: f is random — K(f) ≈ 2^d. Search never terminates.
algorithmic_information_theory.verdict: REJECTED as direct method (uncomputable). But INSPIRES program synthesis with bounded search.
